貫.meaning: A woodpecker mistakes a giant clam for a tree. Tap, tap, tap: it drills a neat round <part>window</part> straight through the <part>shellfish</part>, and the clam peers out, rather pleased with the view. That beak can <kanji>pierce</kanji> anything.
貫.on: The clam hangs a pink <sound>car</sound>nation in its new window.
貫.kun: A <sound>tsu</sound>nami rolls in, the crowd on the beach shouts '<sound>Rah</sound>!', and the woodpecker hides in a <sound>noo</sound>k.

尾.meaning: A dog wants to join the parade but has nothing to wave, so he ties a <part>flag</part> to his back end. It falls off. He glues on a ball of <part>fur</part> from the hairbrush instead; that falls off too. In the end he just wags. The best thing to wave is a <kanji>tail</kanji>.
尾.on: A <sound>bee</sound>tle rides on the wagging tip all the way to the end of the parade.
尾.kun: '<sound>Oh</sound>!' gasps the crowd, as one big wag knocks over the drummer.

漢.meaning: A <part>husband</part> paddles a canoe east for a whole year, flicking <part>water drops</part> off his paddle and cooking <part>grass</part> soup when the snacks run out. When he finally lands, he opens his <part>mouth</part> and reads hello from his notebook of brush-drawn characters. He has reached <kanji>China</kanji>.
漢.on: On the beach, a smiling stranger hands him a pink <sound>car</sound>nation.

剣.meaning: At a <part>campsite</part>, a scout leader toasts marshmallows on a little <part>dagger</part>, but they keep falling in the fire. So he forges a longer blade, then longer still, until he's waving one as tall as the tent. Now his marshmallows hang from a <kanji>sabre</kanji>.
剣.on: His dog watches from her <sound>ken</sound>nel, waiting for one to drop.
剣.kun: A sudden <sound>tsu</sound>nami of rain hits, so he shoos a <sound>roo</sound>k and two <sound>gee</sound>se into the tent.

筒.meaning: A postman cuts <part>bamboo</part> stalks into tubes all the <part>same</part> size, slips a letter inside each one and rolls them down the hills to every farm. One rolls into a pond and floats off like a boat. Each letter travels in its own <kanji>cylinder</kanji>.
筒.on: One rolls straight over a farmer's big <sound>toe</sound>.
筒.kun: '<sound>Tsu</sound>! <sound>Tsu</sound>!' the farmer hisses through his teeth, hopping on one foot.

択.meaning: A sailor shopping for a new <part>anchor</part> lays them all out on the dock and takes the <part>measure</part> of each with a tape: too small, too rusty, too shaped like a duck. In the end she picks the duck one. It was hard to <kanji>choose</kanji>.
択.on: She celebrates with a crunchy <sound>taco</sound> on the dock.
択.kun: The shopkeeper throws in a free <sound>e</sound>gg and shouts '<sound>Rah</sound>!' as she sails off.

棄.meaning: Moving house, a man fills a crate with junk: an old pot <part>lid</part>, a shirt with a hole at the <part>elbow</part>, a <part>comb</part> with no teeth. He leaves it under a <part>tree</part> with a sign saying 'Free!' Nobody takes a thing, not even the squirrels. Some things you just have to <kanji>abandon</kanji>.
棄.on: On top of the pile he leaves the old house <sound>key</sound>.
棄.kun: A stray cat sniffs the crate and drags off a <sound>su</sound>shi roll from the bin beside it.

柔.meaning: A whaler retires and hangs his old <part>harpoon</part> on the apple <part>tree</part> in his garden. Moss grows on it, sparrows nest in it, and the apples below are bruised by nothing harsher than rain. Now he spends his days feeding ducks, as <kanji>tender</kanji> as a ripe peach.
柔.on: He keeps his old medal, a sea-green <sound>jew</sound>el, in the sparrows' nest.
柔.kun: He hums to the baby in the next <sound>ya</sound>rd until it stops its '<sound>wah</sound>' and smiles.
